structured_output.world_model:
E001 (airbench96-style port, 9 epochs) measured acc 0.74297, time 9.43 s, complete, not feasible (below 0.753 by about 1.0 pp). My earlier range hit on both metrics (time 9.43 and acc 0.743), but I voted refutes on H1.1.1; that is consistent, since the port misses 0.753.

Beliefs:
1. Epochs-to-target dominates time (H1). About 1.0 s/epoch including about 0.4 s fixed cost. The port needs roughly 10-11 epochs to clear 0.753, i.e. 10-20% more time. Slope: roughly 0.4-0.6 pp per extra epoch near 9 epochs (diminishing returns), so 9->10 gives about +0.4 to +0.8 pp. Evidence: a single run, 1 pp short.
2. Systems gains. The eager port is likely partly launch-bound: the augment loop does 25 masked copies per epoch, and SGD uses a per-param loop. torch.compile with max-autotune typically gives 5-15% on fp16 convnets. Autotune may leak into timed code (recompiles on shape changes). CUDA graphs would give less than 3%. The accuracy effect is about 0.
3. Fixed costs (prepare, data transfer, whitening eigh, augment) are about 0.3-0.5 s, around 4-5%.
4. Noise: per-seed accuracy std is about 0.2-0.4 pp, so the 3-seed mean std is about 0.15-0.25 pp. Time noise is about 1-2%, with occasional 3% from GPU clocks. Tweaks of 0.1-0.3 pp (EMA, LS, flip) are within noise, so they are mostly inconclusive. Past gains partly regress, so I shade claims downward.
5. Muon and progressive resizing are risky. Muon at batch 2000 with fewer steps likely hurts accuracy at 9 epochs unless tuned. Progressive resizing risks BN-statistics mismatch and a train/test resolution gap, and it needs cuDNN warmup per resolution. Expect an accuracy loss of 0.5-1.5 pp for a saving of about 15-25% of time.

Unsure: the exact step time, whether EMA helps at 9 epochs (the airbench96 EMA is meant for longer runs), and compile-time leakage.

forecasts.reason: Port is 1 pp below the bar, so the rule picks 9->10 epochs; +11% time and about +0.5 pp accuracy, still likely just under 0.753.
Compile plus a fused optimizer likely gives a modest 5-15% gain; autotune leakage and the augment loop limit it, and the 10% threshold is borderline.
EMA gain of about +0.2 pp is within the 3-seed noise, and the extra copies add about 1-2% time.
An identical rerun should give time within about 2% and accuracy within about 0.2 pp; per-seed std about 0.25 pp.
The port already uses 1024x9 with a ragged-free n//bs loop (drops the last 848 images), so there is little to gain; the effect is likely under 0.3 s.
Untuned Muon at batch 2000 gets about half the steps in 9 epochs; I expect lower accuracy and a Newton-Schulz time overhead, so no 10% epoch cut.
The saving is plausibly 10-15%, but the accuracy loss at same epochs is likely 0.3-1 pp, which is more than the 0.2 pp tolerance.

cruxes: What is the real per-seed accuracy std and run-to-run time noise (I005)? It sets the margin above 0.753 and whether small gains are detectable.
Is the eager port launch- or augment-bound, so that compile and a fused optimizer give more than 10%?
How many epochs does the port need to clear 0.753 with margin (about 10 vs 11)? This fixes the baseline that every systems gain is measured against.
